segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Hello. Welcome to Real Easy English from BBC Learning English. I'm Georgie.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil. We're here to help you improve your English with a real conversation in easy English.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: If you want to read along, you can find a text version of this podcast at bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Right, let's start the show. How are you today, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you, Georgie. What are we talking about in this episode?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Today is all about friends. We'll talk a bit about our friends and why they are important.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Great, let's get started.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, Neil, do you have a lot of friends?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, I do have quite a few friends. How about you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, I also have quite a lot of friends. I've lived in different places, so I have

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: made friends in lots of different areas and times of my life

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So Georgie you said that you have lived in lots of places and I know you have lived in Spain So do you have lots of friends in Spain

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, I have a few friends in Spain

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: but now that I live in London,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: it's quite difficult to stay in touch with them.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But actually, one of them is coming to visit this weekend.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Ah, so you try to keep in touch with some of your friends. That means to keep contact with them, to make sure that you stay friends by speaking to them.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, exactly. And if you have a lot of friends, it can be difficult to stay in touch with so many.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: What do you like to do with your friends, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, I like to talk to them mainly. So I like to meet them maybe in a pub or a restaurant or we go to a sports match sometimes and we talk there and have a good time.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: That sounds nice.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How about you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, I'm the same. During the week, I think a nice plan is to go out for dinner with friends.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: At the weekends I like going for a walk or getting a coffee with friends

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You can do both of those at the same time

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah that right Sometimes I meet friends we get a coffee to take away

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: and then go for a walk around the park.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And are you happy about the number of friends you have

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: or would you like to have more or fewer?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I always like making new friends.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: If you start a new hobby or you move to a different place, there are always more people and new people to meet.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I like making friends. What about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, but I like to see my old friends and if I make new friends, I know it's something that happens slowly and that's OK.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Now, we have used this word friends a lot, but there are other words for friends too, aren't there?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes. One is mate. I use mate a lot. We also use pal. So sometimes I refer to my friends that are girls as gal pals.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Gal pals. That's a nice expression.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So Neil, why are friends important to you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Ah yes Good question Friends are important I think because you can be yourself with your friends You don have to pretend if they good friends because they know you as you are

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And that's not the same everywhere that you go in life.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah, that's true.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap the language we learned during the conversation.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We learned mates and pals, which are other words for friends.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We heard keep in touch with, which means see or speak to someone regularly.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We also say stay in touch.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And a few, which means more than two, but not many.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So I have a few friends in Spain, but not many.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Thanks for listening to Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Visit our website for more activities and courses to help you with your English bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Next time, we'll talk about holidays and places we would like to go.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: See you then. Goodbye.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Bye.
